title: Rabbi Elazar ben Teradyon
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 7:4, asking the sages a halakhah concerning seclusion. In the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 1, chapter 2, Rav Sherira wrote that he belonged to the generation of the sages of Yavneh. Hyman suggests that possibly he was the brother of Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon.

notes.text: The statement about the generation of Yavneh is reported from Rav Sherira; the possible brotherhood with Chanina ben Teradyon is Hyman’s conjecture. Neither is an identity merge.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 7:4 directly names Elazar ben Teradyon asking the sages about seclusion with one witness in the morning and another in the evening. The consulted digital Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, question 1, paragraph 6, includes him in a list with Yose the Galilean, Elazar ben Azariah, and Chanina ben Teradyon. Hyman’s exact part-and-chapter numbering has not been independently collated, and the possible brotherhood remains his conjecture.
